items.title: Section: Hope, Seeking, Grief, and Sorrow — The Sorrow Faculty's Own Path Towards Liberation

items.zh: 如經言：於上解脫希、求、憂、慼。云何希？謂修行者作如是念：是處眾聖能具足住。求云何？謂修行者作如是念：我於是處當具足住。慼云何？謂於下劣不生喜足。憂云何？謂於無上心生思慕。此中，預流、一來，於一切種皆圓滿故，建立憂根。若不還果，雖有初二，餘二無故，不立憂根，唯善法欲。
items.en: As the sūtra says: hoping for, seeking, sorrowing over, and grieving for liberation from what lies above. What is hope? A practitioner reflects: this is the place every noble one can fully abide within. What is seeking? A practitioner reflects: I too should come to fully abide in this very place. What is grief? Not feeling satisfied with any inferior attainment. What is sorrow? An intense, longing reflection directed at the unsurpassed attainment. Here, stream-entry and once-returning, being complete in every one of these, establish the sorrow faculty. Non-returning, though it has the first two, lacks the remaining two, and so does not establish the sorrow faculty, having only wholesome aspiration.

items.zh: 問：頗有依止喜根，能捨喜根、憂根、捨根耶？答：有。謂依出離喜根為依止故，捨依耽嗜三根。問：頗有依止憂根，捨憂根耶？答：有。謂依出離為依止故，捨依耽嗜。

items.title: Section: Relinquishing One Kind of Equanimity by Relying on a Deeper One

items.zh: 問：頗有依止捨根，捨捨根耶？答：有。謂依一性捨為依止故，捨依種種性捨。無所依捨為依止故，捨依一性捨。得預流果時，未知欲知根亦滅亦捨，非起而棄，非斷非退。得阿羅漢果時，已知根道理，應知亦爾。
items.en: Question: is there any relying on equanimity to relinquish equanimity? Answer: yes. Relying on the single, uniform equanimity relinquishes the manifold equanimity; relying on the non-reliant equanimity relinquishes the single, uniform equanimity. Upon attaining the fruit of stream-entry, the aspirant's faculty both ceases and is relinquished, yet not through arising and being cast off, nor through severing, nor through regression. Upon attaining arhatship, the same principle applies to the knower's faculty.

items.title: Section: Sharpening Dull Faculties — What a Refined Stream-Enterer Can and Cannot Yet Reach

items.zh: 問：幾補特伽羅有練根耶？答：一切有學；及無學五，退、思、護、住、堪達種性。非諸獨覺，亦非菩薩，性利根故。問：若預流者修練根時，既得練根，亦證一來果耶？答：證。問：亦證不還果耶？答：不證。對治難得故，所應得義極廣大故。
items.en: Question: which practitioners engage in refining the faculties? Answer: every trainee, together with five kinds of one beyond training — those prone to regression, those inclined to end their life, those who safeguard their attainment, those who merely maintain it, and those merely capable of penetrating further. Neither solitary realisers nor bodhisattvas do so, being naturally sharp-natured. Question: for a stream-enterer practising this refinement, does it also bring the fruit of once-returning? Answer: yes. Question: does it also bring non-returning? Answer: no — because the antidote is difficult to attain, and what must be achieved is exceedingly vast.

items.zh: 問：若不還者修練根時，既得練根，亦進離欲耶？答：進。問：亦證阿羅漢果耶？答：不證，由前因故。轉根已後，一切皆證。

items.title: Section: Five Reasons to Refine the Faculties, and What "Complete" Actually Means

items.zh: 問：何故轉根？答：於薄少昇進不生喜足故，為植引發勝定力故，為植多聞力故，為植論議決擇力故，為植觀察甚深法忍力故。問：諸菩薩未知欲知等三根，云何建立？答：於勝解行地，建立初根。於淨增上意樂地等，立第二根。於如來地，立第三根。問：由幾種滿，名學滿耶？答：由三種滿。一、根滿，謂利根。二、定滿，謂八解脫定。三、果滿，謂不還果。若諸無學，得有二滿。一、根滿，謂不動法。二、定滿，如前應知。一切無學，皆由果滿說名為滿。
items.en: Question: why refine the faculties? Answer: from dissatisfaction with only slight progress, and to cultivate superior concentration, extensive learning, skill in debate, and the patient insight of contemplating profound truth. Question: how are a bodhisattva's three faculties of realisation established? Answer: the first is established at the stage of resolute conduct; the second from the first ground onward, at the stage of purified aspiration; the third at the stage of a Tathāgata. Question: by how many completenesses is a trainee's perfection named? Answer: three — completeness of faculty, meaning sharp faculties; completeness of concentration, meaning the eight liberations; and completeness of fruit, meaning non-returning. One beyond training possesses two completenesses explicitly — of faculty, the unshakeable kind, and of concentration, as before. Yet every one beyond training is called complete simply on the strength of fruit-completeness.

items.title: Section: The Four Ways Ordinary Senses Go Untamed

items.zh: 問：如說諸根不調、不守、不護、不防，亦不修習，此差別名有何義耶？答：略說由四因緣，諸根名不調伏。
items.en: Question: scripture speaks of the senses as untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unwarded, and uncultivated — what distinguishes these terms? Answer: in brief, four causes together constitute what is called the senses being untamed.

items.title: Section: Six Sufferings of an Untamed Mind, and the Joy That Comes From Genuine Discipline

items.zh: 謂簡擇力為依止故，於諸境界，若不應縱諸根之者，便起加行令不縱逸。若應縱者，便起加行縱彼諸根，護諸煩惱令不現起。斷對治力為依止故，即於如前所說境界，為性無著，為性煩惱不復現行。若無是四調諸根者，當知彼根名不調伏，由不守故、不護故、不防故、不修故。若有是四調諸根者，當知與彼四種相違，名為調伏乃至修習。云何不調伏者能引眾苦？謂能生六種苦故。一、擾惱住所生苦，二、他所擯黜苦，三、他所譏毀苦，四、追悔所生苦，五、往生惡趣苦，六、生等諸苦。若有諸根善調伏者，當知與此相違，斷六種苦，引諸快樂。
items.en: Relying on discerning power, when the senses should not indulge an object, effort is made to prevent indulgence; when they should, effort is made to let them engage while protecting against affliction arising. Relying on the antidote power that cuts through affliction, engaging that same object without any underlying attachment, and with affliction no longer manifesting at all. Why do untamed senses give rise to great suffering? Because they generate six kinds of suffering: agitated dwelling, being cast out by others, being mocked by others, regret, miserable rebirth, and the ongoing suffering of birth and the rest. Well-tamed senses bring the opposite: these six sufferings cut off, and every joy brought forth.

items.title: Section: How the Three Realms Contain Fourteen Faculties, and How Five Feelings Fold Into Three

items.zh: 問：十四種根、三聚有情，為十四攝三，三攝十四耶？答：三攝十四，非十四攝三。不攝何等？謂外處少分。三聚有情者，謂欲界、色界、無色界。問：五根、三受、為五攝三，三攝五耶？答：更互相攝。
items.en: Question: are the fourteen faculties subsumed by the three groups of beings, or the three groups by the fourteen faculties? Answer: the three groups subsume the fourteen, not the reverse. What is not subsumed? A portion of the external environment. The three groups of beings are those of the desire, form, and formless realms. Question: are the five feeling faculties subsumed by the three kinds of feeling, or the reverse? Answer: they mutually subsume each other.

blocks.text: Sorrow aimed at liberation, refining dull faculties into sharp ones, and the four ways the senses go untamed.
Master Cháng Bǎi: beings hope, seek, worry, and grieve over whether they can free themselves from affliction. The first two fruits have all four; non-returners only hope and seeking.

Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on single-pointed equanimity, one leaves the manifold equanimity towards form. (Untranslated, 0618c05: relying on the joy of renunciation, one abandons the joy, sorrow, and equanimity based on indulgence.)
(Untranslated, 0618c19: a non-returner who refines the faculties also advances in freedom from desire, but does not thereby attain arhatship.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: to see the profound nature of things and accomplish the wisdom of acceptance, one must refine the faculties; reading the Tripiṭaka also refines them.

Four causes: unguarded, unprotected, unwarded, uncultivated. Master Cháng Bǎi: guarding turns inward, keeping the faculties from outer objects; protecting keeps the mind safe when they meet objects; warding is the mind not clinging.
Master Cháng Bǎi: discerning which objects may be engaged belongs to wisdom from hearing and reflection.
"Reading the Tripiṭaka also refines the faculties." Study is not separate from practice.

quiz.q: The English has "liberation from what lies above." What is the problem?
options: no problem: one is to be freed from the upper two realms, as the lecture says
希 should be "demand"
上解脫 is the unsurpassed liberation one longs for, not freedom from something above; the English reverses this
憂慼 should be "anger"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings hope for, seek, worry, and grieve over being able to liberate themselves from affliction. The later clause, a longing for the unsurpassed, confirms the direction: 上解脫 is the goal above, not what one escapes from. "Liberation from what lies above" misplaces it.

quiz.q: Among the fruits, which establish the sorrow faculty, and why?
options: only non-returning establishes it, longing for arhatship being deepest there, while stream-entry and once-returning have not yet longed so deeply and have only aspiration
stream-entry and once-returning, having all four, establish it; non-returning has only two, with wholesome aspiration alone
all four fruits establish it
none establishes it
quiz.why: The treatise says the first two fruits are complete in all four and so establish sorrow; non-returners have only hope and seeking. Master Cháng Bǎi: first and second fruits have all four, a sorrow joined with renunciation; third-fruit noble ones seek arhatship but have left desire-realm desire and have no sorrow.

quiz.q: What is relying on equanimity to relinquish equanimity, and what happens to the aspirant's faculty at stream-entry?
options: the manifold relinquishes the single; the aspirant's faculty is severed and discarded as an affliction
equanimity cannot relinquish itself; the faculty stays
the single relinquishes the manifold, the non-reliant the single; the aspirant's faculty ceases and is relinquished, without severing or regression
joy relinquishes equanimity; the faculty regresses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on the single equanimity, one leaves the manifold equanimity towards form through phenomena; the signless mind samādhi or cessation is the non-reliant equanimity, leaving the single equanimity of the formless attainments. Attaining the first fruit does not sever the aspirant's faculty; it only transforms it.

quiz.q: The English has "the patient insight of contemplating profound truth." How does it compare with the lecture?
options: no: 法忍 is patience with harm, identical to §58, so "insight" is added
no: it should be "legal tolerance"
broadly so: the lecture speaks of contemplating profound nature and attaining the wisdom of acceptance; "patient insight" conveys acceptance rather than endurance
no: it speaks of extensive learning
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to observe the profound nature of phenomena and accomplish the wisdom of acceptance, one must refine the faculties; reading the Tripiṭaka also refines them. 忍 here is acceptance, a kind of wisdom, not endurance. The English "patient insight" points towards that, though "patient" may mislead.

quiz.q: How many causes constitute untamed senses, and how do they relate to the five terms?
options: five causes, each of the five terms naming its own separate cause, 不調 being only one among them, and so the five cannot be gathered under the single heading untamed
four causes: unguarded, unprotected, unwarded, uncultivated, together called untamed
two causes
six causes, one per faculty
quiz.why: The treatise says four causes constitute the untamed. Master Cháng Bǎi: these four are unguarded, unprotected, unwarded, and uncultivated, together called untamed. So 不調 is the heading of the other four, which the English "four causes together" captures.

quiz.q: The English has "indulge" and "let them engage" for 縱. How should 縱 be read?
options: 縱 is letting the faculties meet objects; "let them engage" fits better, "indulge" carrying a negative tone
縱 is indulgence, the treatise saying one may at times enjoy sense pleasures, and so "indulge" is the only correct word
縱 should be "vertical"
縱 should be "punish"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: discerning power belongs to wisdom of hearing and reflection. So this is a choice by wisdom about which objects may be engaged, while guarding against affliction. 縱 here is close to allowing. "Indulge" in English suggests yielding to desire, while "let them engage," used later in the same line, fits better.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi separate guarding, protecting, warding, and cultivating?
options: guarding is ethics, protecting absorption, warding wisdom, cultivating liberation, unrelated to contact
four synonyms
guarding keeps faculties from objects; protecting keeps mind safe at contact; no clinging is warding; no manifestation is cultivating
each belongs to one faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: guarding turns inward, keeping the faculties from outer objects; protecting keeps the mind safe when they meet objects; the mind's not clinging is warding; keeping the seeds of affliction from manifesting is cultivating. So the terms form a progression from discerning power to antidote power.
